decisions.title: No Wolfsberg question set is asked of banks that do not hold the questionnaire
decisions.statement: The questions contained in the Wolfsberg correspondent bank due diligence questionnaire are not asked anywhere in Hazel onboarding. A bank that holds a completed questionnaire may upload it, and that data is run against the CoverBase controls to produce a residual risk score. A bank that does not hold one is asked nothing in its place — it proceeds through the standard due diligence and risk questions, which every applicant answers regardless. A weaker residual risk score is accepted as the consequence.

evidence.excerpt: are these the questions that we are going to require, even though they do have it? So what about the questions in the Wolfberg? Where are those going to go in?
We're not going to address them at all. We're not going to ask for them. That was a decision by Shawn and people above our pay grade that they want to make it as smooth as possible.

So we just decided all together to just take out the Wolfberg. If they have it, great. We'll get it and we'll use that data to create, run it against our controls and get a good residual risk score. If they don't have it, we're not going to ask questions about it.
Yeah, actually.

decisions.confidence_note: The substance is unambiguous and nobody dissented — Joel Olivares answers Diana Plata's direct question flatly, says the group decided it together, and confirms Castaneda was good with it. Two attributes are not: the source names only "Shawn" and Joel reports the call second-hand as made by "Shawn and people above our pay grade", so the owner is inferred to be Shawn Main from the registry; and this reverses the fallback-question-set clause of DEC-001, which warrants a close look before approval.

The mock-up form is the name of the user, their title, the date, and their electronic acknowledgement of what they are doing. The completed acknowledgement is rendered to a PDF and kept for record keeping.

What is not settled is sign-off: Norma Saenz has not heard back on the mock-up and Aaron McWilliams closes the topic with "we'll verify that" (CAND-Q-001). Note also that the source lists signature, name and date, while the mock-up Norma Saenz describes has name, title and date — whether a distinct signature element is additionally required is not resolved.

decisions.title: The e-signature is sent only on the final package, after Hazel's internal review loop closes
decisions.statement: The end-of-journey signature is not triggered when the applicant submits. The sequence is: the bank submits, Hazel reviews internally, the internal review may raise questions and there is back-and-forth with the bank, and only once everything is final does the document go out for e-signature. The version sent for signature is therefore the final document.

Like in our review steps, what we talked about is you submitted, then it's a Hazel review, internal review, then internal review might have some questions. So there will be to and fro. And once that is all final, we are ready and we are seeing like this is all done final. That is a time we will. Send it for resign.

decisions.confidence_note: Shantanu Wadodkar states it as settled — "one thing for sure", "that's what we are putting it together in a workflow" — and Aaron McWilliams does not object, but he is describing what the build team is implementing from feedback received the day before rather than making the call, and nobody is named as having made it. DEC-005 already establishes a single signature at the end; what is new here is the trigger being the close of internal review.

final_takeaways: Nothing in this delta is authoritative. Every item is a candidate for librarian review.
7 candidate decisions, 3 open questions, 8 action items, 6 items deliberately not promoted.

CAND-DEC-001 reverses DEC-001 and is the item to review first: DEC-001 records that a bank without a Wolfsberg questionnaire answers an equivalent question set in Hazel onboarding, and Joel Olivares states here that those questions will not be asked at all. If approved it also moots Q-005, which asks whether CoverBase accepts a fallback answer payload.

CAND-DEC-003 is the only genuinely new NDA mechanic: the end-of-journey signature fires on the final package after Hazel's internal review loop closes, not on submission. Most of the rest of the NDA discussion restates DEC-005.

CAND-Q-003 is in tension with DEC-002. That record says the Hazel-flow NDA satisfies Vanta's requirement so no second NDA is presented; Joel Olivares says here he does not think the Vanta step can be removed at all, because it is the evidence Vanta exists to collect for SOC certification.
CAND-Q-001 may duplicate Q-006. The same mock-up is awaiting the same sign-off, attributed to "Tate" here and to "Jonathan" on 2026-08-03; the source does not establish whether these are one person.

CAND-DEC-007 is low confidence and partially answers Q-010: Shantanu Wadodkar calls the Zeb scope split "tentatively figured out" and says the real structuring discussion waits on Zeb's formal paperwork.
blocking_reasons: All candidates require librarian approval before any record or ticket can be created.
CAND-DEC-001 carries supersedes_id DEC-001. Approving it as a fresh decision rather than a supersession would leave two contradictory records about whether a fallback question set exists.

CAND-DEC-002 and DEC-005 are both gated on a sign-off that has not arrived (CAND-Q-001), and the source is internally inconsistent about whether a distinct signature element sits alongside name, title and date.
CAND-DEC-005 cannot be built as recorded until CAND-Q-002 identifies which document at the documents step stays mandatory.
The build team still has no Azure/Databricks tenant access — the environment is built but invites are blocked on Nathan's approval (ACT-004).
